001: Shota, what kind of career do you want to build at this company?
Well, first I want to aim for project manager and gain experience.
That's a wonderful goal. What specific skills do you want to develop?
Leadership and the communication skills to bring a team together.
I see. I'm learning a lot from this too. Let's do our best together.
Thank you. Yuki, I'd really like to hear your opinion as well.
002: Lately, is there a moment where you feel your own growth?
Well, negotiations that used to be difficult for me have gradually become smoother.
That's a big improvement. Was there something that triggered it?
I think it's because I started putting into practice the preparation method I learned from a senior colleague.
I see. So the fundamentals really are important.
Yes. By thoroughly mastering the basics, I've become more adaptable.
003: When thinking about your career plan, what do you value most?
I want to focus my efforts in an area where my interests and the company's needs align.
That's an important perspective. What specific areas are you interested in?
I'm drawn to work like developing new markets or being a bridge with overseas partners.
That's interesting. Do you have any future plans in that area?
First, I want to further polish my language skills and join an overseas project.
004: Over this past year, how do you think your skills have changed?
I feel that my data analysis skills have improved especially.
That's reassuring. How did you go about acquiring them?
In addition to in-house training, I took online courses on my own initiative.
That effort is impressive. How will you apply it to your future work?
I want to actively use those skills in developing marketing strategies.
005: Can you tell me about your long-term career vision?
Eventually, I'd like to be involved in developing the next generation of talent.
That's wonderful. Why did you become interested in mentoring?
Because I was able to grow thanks to the support of many people, and I want to give back.
That's a great way of thinking. What rewards do you find in mentoring?
I think being able to see people's growth up close is the greatest joy.
006: When you hit a wall at work, how do you overcome it?
I try not to deal with it alone, and instead consult with trusted colleagues or my boss.
That's a good approach. What changes when you talk it out?
By getting an objective opinion, I can notice new perspectives.
I see. It's definitely more efficient than thinking alone.
Yes. And having them help think through solutions together is also reassuring.
007: For your future career, is there anything you want to challenge yourself with?
I'd like to use the company's internal transfer system to gain experience in a new department.
That's ambitious. What kind of department are you interested in?
I'm interested in the overseas division, which is closely related to my current work.
What skills do you want to acquire there?
I want to develop an international mindset and cross-cultural communication skills.
008: For self-improvement, what do you usually do?
I read business books and attend industry seminars.
That's a great habit. Is there a book that particularly influenced you?
A book on leadership I read recently was very helpful.
What points from that book stood out to you?
Learning through concrete examples how important it is to bring out the strength of a team.
009: To achieve your career goals, what do you consider most important?
I think it's giving my full effort to the work in front of me.
That's fundamental, and yet very important.
Yes. I believe that accumulating small successes leads to confidence.
I want to follow that attitude. What are your future goals?
In five years, I want to be leading a team as a fully capable leader.
010: How do you maintain your motivation for work?
It's about cherishing the moments when I can feel my own growth.
Specifically, when do you feel that growth?
I feel a sense of fulfillment when I overcome new challenges or when I'm thanked.
That's wonderful. I want to value that feeling too.
Let's both do our best to keep growing.
